items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Cecil and Fess Williams had copied from Ted Lewis.

ctx.x: Scott played dances on percentage the same as most travelling orchestras did. The percentage was 60 % for the orchestra and 40% for the promoter of the dance. Lloyd paid me and the rest of the musicians $17.00 for our part and he must have had twice that much for himself and

his brother Cecil who stood in front of the orchestra with a top hat on his head like Ted Lewis. That was the most money I had ever made in one night and I never thought that Lloyd had cheated me out of anything if he took a bigger cut from the percentage because he had the responsibility of transportation and other things. I never expected to find another leader like Clarence Paige who counted the money out in packages of ten and gave everyone the same amount from a percentage dance and then asked everyone for…

But I was so happy about the money I received from Lloyd Scott after the first job I did with the group that I saw myself having a bankroll large enough to choke an elephant in a few days. The next job we did, I received $ 7.00 but that was not at all bad for those days. My bankroll did not grow as I thought it would after the first night's pay, but I was happy because I was with a bunch of musicians that had been some places and had musical ideas that I had not experienced before.
